title: 1912 The post office was built, the clock was installed in 1913
description: This two-storey Romanesque building was built in 1912 by the Federal Government to serve as a post office, jail, and armoury. It is the most distinctive structure on the west side of Main Street, Hartland, overlooking the scenic Saint John River Valley. The building became a local historic landmark, playing important roles as a military training centre during both World Wars and as a community gathering place. The second-floor assembly room was managed by the Militia Department. The clock was added in 1913. Today, the building houses the Dr. Walter Chestnut Library.
